newsitem.title: USA: U.S., N.Korean, S.Korean officials meet in New York.
newsitem.headline: U.S., N.Korean, S.Korean officials meet in New York.

text.p: U.S., North Korean and South Korean officials met in New York on Friday, apparently to continue discussions on a proposal for four-way talks on the future of the Korean peninsula.
State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said it was "just a routine meeting" and declined to discuss the agenda or name the participants.

But the meeting comes on the heels of a briefing that the United States and South Korea gave North Korean officials in New York on March 5 on the proposal, and a follow-up meeting there between the three countries on March 26.

The proposal was launched a year ago by U.S. President Bill Clinton and South Korean President Kim Young-sam. The talks, which would bring in China, would aim for a permanent peace in Korea to replace the current truce.

At the March 26 meeting, North Korean officials also raised the issue of the severe food shortages their country is suffering. The United States has given Pyongyang limited food aid but says that issue is unrelated to the talks proposal.
